name: Cisco ASA syslog
description: Cisco ASA's LINA syslog: CLI command and configuration-change auditing, connection build/teardown, local-database user management and discarded-request events, normalized by the Splunk Add-on for Cisco ASA's cisco:asa stanza. One feed for the cisco:asa sourcetype.
source: Splunk Add-on for Cisco ASA (Splunk_TA_cisco-asa) cisco:asa props.conf, transforms.conf and lookups, read from a live instance; Cisco Secure Firewall ASA Series Syslog Messages guide; Splunk Common Information Model Network Traffic, Intrusion Detection and Change data models.

feed.label: Cisco ASA Syslog
feed.description: Cisco ASA's LINA-engine syslog: one line per %ASA-<level>-<id> event, normalized by the Splunk Add-on for Cisco ASA. This pack documents the eleven message ids the sampled attack_data actually carries: CLI auditing, connection build/teardown, local-database user management and a discarded request.

message_id.label: Message id
message_id.description: The numeric id in the %ASA-<level>-<id> token, for example 302013; picks which other fields the line carries.

log_level.label: Syslog level
log_level.description: The syslog priority (0 to 7) in the %ASA-<level>-<id> token; a transport-layer severity, not Cisco's own event severity.

severity_level.label: Syslog level name
severity_level.description: The RFC 5424 name of the syslog priority (emergencies, alert, critical ... debugging), looked up from log_level. Despite the name it grades the syslog transport priority, not the event.

level_description.label: Syslog level meaning
level_description.description: A one-line gloss of the syslog priority (for example Informational messages only), looked up from log_level. On this sourcetype the description field holds this, not a summary of the event.

vendor_severity.label: Vendor severity
vendor_severity.description: Cisco's own severity word (for example Informational, Attack) looked up from signature_id.

severity.label: Severity
severity.description: The CIM-normalized severity word: a literal for four message ids (106016, 106017, 400032, 110003, 405001, 212011), else filled from the same signature_id lookup that sets vendor_severity.

action.label: Action
action.description: The CIM-normalized verb for what ASA did (allowed, blocked, teardown, executed, ...), from a lookup keyed on the raw action token or on message_id.

vendor_action.label: Vendor action
vendor_action.description: Cisco's own action verb before CIM normalization (built, denied, discarded, executed, ...), lower-cased; a literal (blocked, flow) for two message-id groups.

category.label: Signature category
category.description: The vendor category of a matched signature; a literal for three message-id groups (DOS, Spoofing, Attempted Information Leak), else passed through.

signature.label: Signature name
signature.description: The name of the intrusion or condition the event reports; a literal for a set of message ids, else the extracted signature.

signature_id.label: Signature id
signature_id.description: The unique id of the signature or event code; the key the vendor_severity/severity lookup matches on. Equal to message_id itself on four message ids.

ids_type.label: IDS type
ids_type.description: Which kind of detector raised the event. A fixed literal (network) on every cisco:asa record.

status.label: Change status
status.description: Whether a configuration or account change succeeded; success is a literal for a fixed set of message ids, otherwise passed through.

result.label: Result
result.description: The vendor-specific detail of a change's outcome; the literal command text for message id 111009, otherwise the extracted result phrase.

reason.label: Termination reason
reason.description: Why a connection was torn down, for example the TCP flag that ended it; carried on the 302014/302016 teardown messages.

teardown_initiator.label: Teardown initiator
teardown_initiator.description: Which side of the connection sent the packet that tore it down; carried on the 302014 teardown message. The syslog guide names the field without enumerating its values, so no values table is written for it.

session_id.label: Session id
session_id.description: Ties together the records of one session.

direction.label: Direction
direction.description: Which way the packet travelled (inbound, outbound); egress is normalized to outbound.

transport.label: Transport
transport.description: The OSI layer 4 protocol of the traffic (icmp, tcp, udp), lower-cased.

protocol.label: Network protocol
protocol.description: The OSI layer 3 protocol; on this sourcetype it collapses to ip whenever transport is tcp or udp (or message id 338301), and to icmp for icmp traffic. Not the same axis as transport.

protocol_version.label: Protocol version
protocol_version.description: The IP version of the traffic, from a lookup keyed on protocol and communication_protocol.

communication_protocol.label: Address family
communication_protocol.description: ipv4 or ipv6, worked out by pattern-matching whichever of src_ip, dest_ip, src or dest is populated. A TA-internal helper, not a named CIM or Cisco field.

bytes.label: Bytes
bytes.description: Total bytes handled; the literal bytes field if present, else bytes_in plus bytes_out.

packets.label: Packets
packets.description: Total packets handled; the literal packets field if present, else packets_in plus packets_out.

duration.label: Duration
duration.description: Connection or session lifetime in seconds, computed from the day/hour/minute/second components the extraction pulls out of the human-readable duration string.

duration_component.label: Duration component
duration_component.description: One unit (day, hour, minute or second) of the connection lifetime string; four columns that only make sense summed together as duration.

dvc.label: Reporting device
dvc.description: The device that logged the event; aliased from Splunk's own host field, not read from the message text.

original_device_ip.label: Original device address
original_device_ip.description: The IP address of the device that generated the event, for the five 430001-430007 message ids where ASA reports on another device's behalf; distinct from src_ip/dest_ip, which are traffic endpoints.

original_device_time.label: Original device time
original_device_time.description: The generating device's own timestamp string, kept separate from _time. Falls back to strftime(_time) for the same 430001-430007 message ids when the device did not supply its own.

dest.label: Destination
dest.description: The remote host of the traffic; an IP address or hostname depending on message id, with a fallback chain across dest, dest_ip, dest_host and assigned_ipv4.

dest_ip.label: Destination IP
dest_ip.description: The IP address of the destination.

dest_host.label: Destination hostname
dest_host.description: The destination's hostname, populated only for the message ids that report on a named host rather than a bare address. Not a Network Traffic CIM field; the TA's own convention pairing with dest.

dest_interface.label: Destination interface
dest_interface.description: The interface listening remotely or receiving packets locally.

dest_port.label: Destination port
dest_port.description: The destination port of the traffic; forced to 0 for icmp. On the 710002/710003/710005/710006 discarded-request messages it comes from the raw service token rather than its own capture.

dest_public_port.label: Destination public port
dest_public_port.description: The destination port on the public (outside/untranslated) leg of a NAT, alongside dest_port and dest_translated_port. Not a Network Traffic CIM field; forced to 0 for icmp like the other port fields.

dest_translated_ip.label: Destination translated IP
dest_translated_ip.description: The NATed IPv4 or IPv6 address a packet has been sent to.

dest_translated_port.label: Destination translated port
dest_translated_port.description: The NATed port a packet has been sent to; forced to 0 for icmp.

dest_translated_host.label: Destination translated hostname
dest_translated_host.description: The hostname form of dest_translated_ip, when ASA names rather than addresses the mapped destination. Not a Network Traffic CIM field.

dest_user.label: Destination user
dest_user.description: The user identity associated with the destination side of the flow, for example identity-based firewall mapping. Not a Network Traffic CIM field; the TA's directional pairing of user.

dest_nt_domain.label: Destination NT domain
dest_nt_domain.description: The Windows/AD domain qualifying dest_user, on messages that report an AD-authenticated destination identity.

src.label: Source
src.description: The client requesting the connection; an IP address or hostname depending on message id.

src_ip.label: Source IP
src_ip.description: The IP address of the source.

src_host.label: Source hostname
src_host.description: The source's hostname, populated only for message ids that report on a named host. Not a Network Traffic CIM field.

src_interface.label: Source interface
src_interface.description: The interface listening locally or sending packets remotely.

src_port.label: Source port
src_port.description: The source port of the traffic; forced to 0 for icmp.

src_public_port.label: Source public port
src_public_port.description: The source port on the public leg of a NAT, alongside src_port and src_translated_port. Not a Network Traffic CIM field.

src_translated_ip.label: Source translated IP
src_translated_ip.description: The NATed IPv4 or IPv6 address a packet has been sent from.

src_translated_port.label: Source translated port
src_translated_port.description: The NATed port a packet has been sent from; forced to 0 for icmp.

src_translated_host.label: Source translated hostname
src_translated_host.description: The hostname form of src_translated_ip. Not a Network Traffic CIM field.

src_user.label: Source user
src_user.description: The user identity associated with the source side of the flow. Not a Network Traffic CIM field; the TA's directional pairing of user.

user.label: User
user.description: The user tied to the event: src_user or dest_user for a fixed set of message ids and directions, else the extracted user (an admin CLI username on the change/session messages this pack sampled).

ip_address.label: Assigned IP (alias source)
ip_address.description: The underlying field the IP column aliases from; seen on the same address-assignment message ids as assigned_ip. Its own extraction was not independently observed, only the alias.

assigned_ip.label: Assigned IP
assigned_ip.description: The IPv4 or IPv6 address ASA assigned to a client, for example over VPN or DHCP relay.

group.label: Group
group.description: A AAA or VPN group policy name, aliased from the raw Group field.

rule.label: Rule
rule.description: The rule or access-list that decided the action taken.

acl.label: ACL
acl.description: The access-list or rule id, same value as rule.

app.label: Application protocol
app.description: The application protocol of the traffic; a literal (VPN, ASA, WebVPN, Firewall, SNMP) for six message-id groups, else the extracted app.

vendor.label: Vendor
vendor.description: A fixed literal, Cisco, on every record.

product.label: Product
product.description: A fixed literal, ASA, on every record.

vendor_product.label: Vendor product
vendor_product.description: The vendor and product of the device generating the event; a fixed literal, Cisco ASA.

vendor_class.label: Vendor class
vendor_class.description: A message-id-keyed classification Cisco's own lookup adds. The lookup's mechanism was confirmed live; its value table was not sampled, so no values are written here.

vendor_definition.label: Vendor definition
vendor_definition.description: A message-id-keyed free-text definition from the same lookup as vendor_class. Not sampled; no values table.

change_type.label: Change type
change_type.description: The category of a configuration or account change, such as filesystem or AAA, from Cisco's own change-analysis lookup keyed by message_id.

change_class.label: Change class
change_class.description: A coarse change classifier from the same change-analysis lookup, keyed by message_id.

change_description.label: Change description
change_description.description: A short, message-id-specific description of what changed, from the same change-analysis lookup.

command.label: Command
command.description: The command that initiated a change; parent_process_name for message id 111010 (ASA labels the executed command as the parent process), otherwise the extracted command.

object.label: Object
object.description: The name of the object a change affected; a per-message-id literal (src, command, user, "user account", process_name) for six message ids, else the extracted object or object_id.

object_id.label: Object id
object_id.description: The affected object's own id, such as a user account name; a literal for two message-id groups, else coalesce(object_id, object).

object_attrs.label: Object attributes
object_attrs.description: The attributes and values a change touched, for example username, user privilege, encrypted password; a literal for three message-id groups (502101/502102, 502103, 505009), else the extracted object_attrs.

object_category.label: Object category
object_category.description: A generic class for the changed object (filesystem, command, configuration, user), a literal for four message ids, else the extracted object_category.

object_path.label: Object path
object_path.description: Where the changed object lives; the fixed word local (the on-box user database) on the 502101/502102 local-database messages this pack sampled.

object_type.label: Object type
object_type.description: Which kind of thing object names (object, user, policy, context or module), from the same change-analysis lookup as change_class, keyed by message_id.

type.label: Event type
type.description: A coarse classifier (unknown, event, alert) for three message ids, else whatever type the extraction already set.

ssl_is_valid.label: SSL validity
ssl_is_valid.description: Whether an SSL/TLS check passed; failed and validated are normalized to false/true, other raw values pass through unchanged.

privilege_level.label: Privilege level
privilege_level.description: The exec privilege level (0 to 15) a user account was created or deleted with, on the 502101/502102 local-database messages.

old_privilege_level.label: Old privilege level
old_privilege_level.description: The privilege level a user held before a 502103 privilege-level-change event.

new_privilege_level.label: New privilege level
new_privilege_level.description: The privilege level a user was changed to, on a 502103 privilege-level-change event.

encrypted_password.label: Encrypted password
encrypted_password.description: The Encpass token on the 502101/502102 local-database messages. ASA itself always writes this as a fixed string of asterisks; it is never the real hash.

process_name.label: Process name
process_name.description: The application or process name in the message text; "N/A" on the 111010 configuration-change sample this pack read, since command-line CLI sessions do not name an application.

parent_process_name.label: Parent process name
parent_process_name.description: The quoted command text at the end of a 111010 configuration-change message; ASA's own label calls this the process's parent, but the EVAL for command reads it as the command that was run.

zone.label: Local-host zone
zone.description: The security-context or interface name a local-host session belonged to, on the 609001/609002 built/teardown-local-host messages. A different capture than src_interface/dest_interface, which name traffic-flow interfaces rather than a host's own zone.

cisco:asa.description: Cisco ASA's LINA-engine syslog as the Splunk Add-on for Cisco ASA (Splunk_TA_cisco-asa, installed on the dev instance) indexes it: one line per %ASA-<level>-<id> event, CIM field aliases, EVAL-calculated fields and five Cisco-shipped lookups keyed on message_id, signature_id or log_level.
cisco:asa.note: attack_data_cisco_asa_generic_cisco_asa_generic_logs, the sample this pack read (splunk/attack_data datasets/cisco_asa/generic and arcane_door), carries eleven distinct message ids: CLI command/config-change auditing (111008, 111009, 111010), an account lockout (113006), TCP connection build/teardown (302013, 302014), local-database user management (502101, 502102, 502103), a local-host teardown (609002) and a discarded TCP request (710005). The other ~190 message ids the REPORT stanza extracts were not exemplified in this sample and are not documented here.

time_no_year.text: TIME_FORMAT on cisco:asa is %b %d %H:%M:%S, which has no %Y, yet the message text does carry a year (for example Nov 18 2025) and the samples this pack read show _time picking that year up correctly; treat this as unconfirmed for any event where indexing lags far enough that Splunk's own default-year fallback could disagree with the text.

severity_namespace.text: log_level, severity_level, vendor_severity, severity and description look like restatements of one fact but come from two different lookups keyed on two different fields (log_level, and signature_id); severity_level and description grade the syslog transport priority, not the event Cisco detected.

protocol_layers.text: transport, protocol, protocol_version and communication_protocol all sound like the wire protocol. transport is layer 4 (tcp, udp, icmp); protocol collapses to ip or icmp on this sourcetype, not a transport name; protocol_version and communication_protocol both mean IP version, from a lookup and a pattern match respectively.

nat_ports.text: src_port, src_public_port and src_translated_port (and the dest equivalents) can each hold a different port for one NATed flow; filtering on the wrong one silently returns nothing.

ids_look_alike.text: message_id, signature_id, session_id and object_id are four unrelated identifier spaces on this sourcetype; a bare number is not evidence of which one it is.

names_not_stable.text: user, src_user and dest_user are whatever name ASA's own auth source supplied; the same person can appear under different strings across a domain rename or a different auth backend.

password_masked.text: encrypted_password is always the literal ***** in the 502101/502102 message text ASA itself writes; it never carries a real hash, so it is only useful to confirm that a password field was touched, not what the password was.
